scope: Reusable geometry archetypes shared by the Texas and Minnesota 3D demo projects. An archetype is a shape and its import metadata. It carries no place, no owner, no operator, and no measured value; a placement binds identity from a server artifact and never from this catalog.

runtime.reason: Single-file binary glTF loads without sidecar fetches, is supported by the deck.gl/loaders.gl stack already present in the browser bundle (@deck.gl/mesh-layers and @loaders.gl/gltf arrive transitively with deck.gl), and keeps one artifact per archetype for checksum pinning. Any other renderer, three.js included, is a new dependency and a separate decision: three is in neither web/package.json nor web/package-lock.json today.
runtime.textures: KTX2/Basis where a texture is required; plain PNG is acceptable for a first pass
runtime.compression: Draco geometry compression optional; if used it must be declared per file and the uncompressed triangle budget still applies

transform.pivotDefinition: Origin sits on the ground plane at the footprint centre: y=0 is the base, x/z centred on the footprint rectangle. A model whose pivot floats or sits at a bounding-box centre cannot be placed on terrain without per-asset correction.
transform.orientation: Author facing -Z. The placement pipeline applies yaw; the model must not bake a site-specific rotation.

footprint.definition: length is the -Z extent at author orientation, width the X extent. The rectangle is the selection and collision proxy; it is nominal author geometry, not a surveyed parcel boundary.
footprint.tolerance: Rendered geometry must fit inside its declared footprint rectangle within 5%.

connectors.definition: Named empty nodes marking where a line or feeder attaches. A connector is a geometric attachment point only; it asserts no electrical connectivity, rating, or energisation.

roles.NONE: Archetype exposes no electrical attachment point

statusMaterials.definition: A shared material slot the runtime tints from the server-asserted label carried by the placement's artifact. The model ships neutral; it must not bake a status colour.
statusMaterials.note: There is deliberately no decorative or 'illustrative' state. The narrative-IA contract removed it because nothing on master asserts it, and a label the browser invents would breach the 00-overview browser/server boundary.
statusMaterials.pairing: Every colour must be paired with a readable text label and a glyph or pattern; colour alone never carries the claim.

budgets.lodRule: lod1 <= 40% of lod0 triangles, lod2 <= 12%. lod2 must stay recognisable in silhouette at statewide zoom.
budgets.note: Budgets are per archetype instance as authored. Scene-level streaming, culling, and instancing are 2WKG-371's problem, not this contract's; the scene budget is stated so an archetype author knows the ceiling they share.

deliverables.licence: Every delivered model must state a licence that permits redistribution in this repository. A model derived from a third-party asset must name that asset and its licence in source_of_shape.
deliverables.storage: Binary model files are not committed to Git. They are produced and stored per the asset-pipeline work item (2WKG-374 Minnesota / 2WKG-320 Texas); this contract governs their shape, not their hosting.

crossProjectReuse.rule: Geometry is shared; identity is not. The same archetype_id may be instanced in the Texas and Minnesota scenes.
crossProjectReuse.identityRule: A Minnesota placement takes its id, coordinates, coverage, provenance, and status label from an accepted Minnesota server artifact. It must never inherit a Texas placement's identity, nor be relabelled from the ACTIVSg2000 synthetic case, which is Texas-shaped synthetic topology.
crossProjectReuse.placementPrerequisite: Minnesota placement is gated on accepted Minnesota coverage (2WKG-364 inventory, 2WKG-367 adapter). Until an accepted artifact exists, an archetype may be previewed in a catalogue view but must not be positioned as Minnesota infrastructure.

archetypes.limit: A tower is scene furniture. It never implies a real circuit, rating, energisation, or a Minnesota network; topology scenes stay disabled until the network decision gate accepts a solver-complete source.
Equipment count and layout are generic. They assert no bay configuration, capacity, or ownership.
A generic installation silhouette. It depicts no real facility, perimeter, or asset disposition.
Bed count, service level, and backup generation are not represented and must not be inferred.
Process stages are illustrative geometry, not a treatment-capacity or service-population claim.

archetypes.semantic_name: Coal plant and retiring plant site
archetypes.limit: Retirement state is a server-asserted attribute of the placement, never a variant baked into the mesh.
A generic module massing. It is not a vendor design, a licensed reactor, or a sited project, and carries no permitting status.
Hall count implies no MW demand. Load comes from an artifact, not from geometry.
A repeating block used for texture and scale. It represents no census population, household count, or customer count.
Generic massing for district context only.
Depicts no process, output, or emissions profile.
Unit count is generic and implies no capacity, heat rate, or fuel arrangement.
Rotor motion, if animated, is decorative. It must never be driven by, or read as, a generation or wind-speed value.
Panel rows are a tiled pattern; they encode no array size, tracking mode, or output.
Container count implies no MWh, no duration, and no state of charge. The demo has no stateful storage model.
Stall count implies no charger rating or utilisation.
Depicts no shelter designation, capacity, or emergency role; those are artifact attributes.
